hook: SCP-826 is a pair of dragon-headed bookends that turn a room into the world of whatever book they hold. The main page is short and rule-focused; the actual trips into books are recorded in a separate experiment log that this page only points to.
whyItMatters:
It is a compact, rule-driven take on the old wish to step inside a story, written as a set of mechanics rather than an adventure. The Safe label, a simple keypad safe and a weekly code change sit oddly beside an effect that can permanently erase a person into fiction.

Because the rules are so clear, the entry invites readers to imagine their own test runs, which is presumably what the pointer to the log is for.
thingsToNotice:
The rules hide a clock. The traveler lands at a random point in the plot, possibly near its end, and has to locate the bookends somewhere in the setting before the story finishes; the object even moves itself to places where books are kept, so the search target is a book inside a book.

If the story ends first, the plot restarts and the traveler is absorbed as a background character with no memory of a life outside. The way back is equally specific: take the book out from between the dragons and walk out of whatever room you are in, and both you and the containment room return to normal.
